Our guiding principle

To connect people across languages and cultures, building a world of inclusion, understanding, and limitless communication.

Why we exist

Shiloh & Smith was established to bridge critical communication divides during multilateral diplomacy, regional trade treaties, peace negotiations and international development conferences.

Owned, not rented

We operate fully owned, calibrated inventory — ISO soundproof booths, DIS hardware and infrared channels — so the system at your summit is the system we maintain every week.

Common questions

Before you ask

Yes. We route the physical floor and booth audio into Zoom Multilingual Audio Channels, Microsoft Teams or Webex, and into dedicated RSI platforms such as Interprefy and KUDO — with a remote audio monitor engineer on duty for the whole session.
Infrared distribution scales to 3,000+ delegates. Because IR is line-of-sight light rather than radio, it is also secure — the signal does not pass through walls, which is why it is the standard for confidential plenaries.
Regularly. We deploy across Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and the DRC, handling cross-border transport, ATA Carnet and customs documentation ourselves.
Interpreters and technicians work under strict diplomatic confidentiality and NDAs. Booth audio is not recorded unless you instruct us to record it, and translated documents are handled under the same terms.
Event dates and venue, estimated delegates, the languages required, and any terms of reference or tender documents you already have. The form below collects exactly that — nothing more.
